text:
alex: Heads-up: canary for multi-tenant serving shows a ~2% p99 latency regression after last tensor-pool patch. nvprof/NSight traces point at repeated small cudaMallocs during forward for the logits scratchpad.

maria: ugh, saw that too in telemetry. KV cache tail latency also spiked for some sessions. probably memory churn + fragmentation.

jin: I grabbed a profiler dump during a high-load replay. snippet below (nvtx names mapped):
```
[Forward] allocate logits_scratchpad 1.2MB (cudaMalloc)
[Forward] free logits_scratchpad 1.2MB (cudaFree)
[Forward] allocate logits_scratchpad 1.2MB (cudaMalloc)
... repeated per token batch
[KV] retain 4MB entries, no eviction
```
Seems the scratchpad is being allocated per-request instead of reusing the per-stream pooled buffer.

alex: That matches my hypothesis. We changed the allocation site to "on-demand per-forward" to avoid oversized precommit, but we forgot to hook the reuse path for variable batch shapes.

maria: The interesting bit: when batch sizes are uneven (mixed short/long), the workspace sizing path returns exact sizes and bypasses size-class pooling. So fragmentation + many small mallocs occur.

jin: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) add a size-class fallback for scratchpads with power-of-two buckets up to 8MB, 2) keep a per-stream single logits buffer and mark it sticky across model variants, 3) implement a fast-path that returns a borrowed buffer instead of malloc/free.

perf-bot: Canary results: before-change p99=58ms, after-change p99=59.2ms (+2.0%). Memory churn metric "malloc_ops/s" increased 6x on canary. Link: https://perf.redwood/canary/1891234567

alex: I like jin's plan. Low-risk immediate change: re-enable pooled borrow path for logits/scratchpad, but keep the conservative sizing calculation. We should also add a telemetry flag to measure "borrow vs malloc" rate.

maria: Also need an OOM mitigation lane: if borrow fails or pool empty, we should trigger KV-cache LRU eviction before falling back to malloc. Otherwise we risk full device OOM under burst.

jin: I'll sketch the patch:
```diff
- auto buf = cuda_malloc(sz);
+ auto buf = pool.borrow(sz_class(sz));
+ if (!buf) {
+   kv_cache.evict_oldest(1); // try to free some workspace via KV
+   buf = pool.borrow(sz_class(sz));
+ }
+ if (!buf) buf = cuda_malloc(sz);
```
We also need to add unit tests that simulate rapid alternating batch sizes to assert <1% malloc_ops/s.

alex: Good. Also add a canary that forces mixed batch shapes to exercise the corner. Put runtime flag `--pool-force-sizeclass` to enable during initial rollout.

maria: Telemetry additions: counters: pool.borrow_count, pool.miss_count, malloc_ops, kv_evict_count, per_stream_shared_bytes. Add traces for per-forward allocations.

perf-bot: Note: rolling back the previous patch removed an unrelated eager compact path which reduced fragmentation. If we reintroduce pooling we should keep that compacting heuristic.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary cluster has been tagged "tensor-pool-patch-2" and scheduled for a 10% traffic split. Use caution.

alex: Action items: jin -> open PR implementing size-class borrow + KV-evict fallback; maria -> add telemetry counters + canary config; alex -> run replay with mixed shapes and attach nvprof. Target: patch + canary today, full rollout after 24h of stable metrics.

maria: TL;DR: regression caused by bypassing pooling for variable batch shapes leading to malloc/free churn. Fix = size-class pools + per-stream sticky logits buffer + KV-evict OOM path.

alex: assigning jira INF-8723, ping me if blocked. :thumbsup:
